transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… mostly I’m just really tired. Like, sleep doesn’t seem to fix it. Even small stuff, like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class, feels like a lot.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I wouldn’t say sad exactly. Just kind of worn out, I guess.
Have you been enjoying things you normally like to do?
Not really. I mean… I still try sometimes, but things I usually like—sketching, cooking, yoga, even tennis with a friend—just don’t really pull me in lately. I kind of stopped caring about them.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things that used to give you pleasure?
Yeah… I think so. I’ve kind of stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself—sketching, cooking, yoga… even tennis with a friend. It just doesn’t really do much for me lately.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?
I don’t think so… not really. I mean, nothing specific comes to mind.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?
Yeah… I guess it’s been kind of off. Some days I’ll realize I’ve only had coffee and a few bites of something. My jeans are a little looser too, but I wasn’t trying to lose weight.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?
Yeah… a bit. I’ll have my planning app open and just stare at it, like I can’t decide if I should do a class assignment, pay a bill, or start dinner. Then I end up not doing any of it for a while.
Have you been feeling restless or slowed down lately?
Yeah… more slowed down, I think. On those days it’s like I’m moving through wet cement. Even answering my spouse about something simple can take me… longer than it should.
Have you been having any thoughts about harming yourself?
No… not really. I mean, I’ve felt low, but I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um… I guess about three months. It’s been this quieter stretch where I just haven’t felt like myself.
Have you been experiencing these feelings almost every day?
I’m not sure I’d say almost every day… it’s hard to track. It’s been pretty often, but I don’t really know exactly.
Would you say these feelings have been present for most of the day?
I don’t really know… maybe some days, but I haven’t been keeping track like that.
Would you say your feelings of being worn out and disinterested have been mild, or have they significantly impacted your daily life?

It’s… not severe, I guess, but it has gotten in the way. I’ve fallen behind on my certificate coursework, and stuff like bills and meals and house things kind of pile up. My spouse has had to help more, and I haven’t really been keeping up with friends or art stuff like I usually would.
Would you describe your current state as feeling somewhat down but still able to function, or has it been more intense and significantly interfering with your daily life?

I guess it’s more than just “somewhat down.” I’m still doing some things, but it’s been interfering. I’ve gotten behind on my certificate work, and bills and meals and house stuff pile up. My spouse has had to help more, and I’ve kind of pulled back from friends and art things.
Would you say that your feelings of tiredness and disinterest have been consistently present, or have there been periods where you felt somewhat better?
There are little moments where I feel a bit better, I guess, but mostly it’s been this quieter low stretch. The tiredness and not caring about much has been going on for… maybe about three months.
Would you say that your low mood and lack of interest in activities are moderate or severe?

I’d say mild… maybe moderate at times, but not severe. I just kind of stopped caring about things I usually like—sketching, cooking, yoga, going to galleries, even tennis with a friend. It feels muted, I guess.
Would you say that your current low mood and lack of interest are causing significant distress or impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like I can’t do anything, but I’ve fallen behind on my certificate work, and stuff like bills, meals, house things just kind of piles up. My spouse has had to pick up more, and I haven’t really been keeping up with friends or art commitments like I normally would.
Would you say that your low mood and lack of interest in activities are interfering with your daily life more than half of the time?

Yeah… probably more than half the time. It’s not constant every second, but most days I’m not really keeping up. I’ve fallen behind on my coursework, and things like bills or meals or house stuff just pile up. My spouse has had to cover more, and I’ve kind of pulled back from friends and art things.
Would you say that your current low mood and lack of interest are significantly impacting your ability to work or take care of daily responsibilities?

Yeah… it is. I’m not working, but with my certificate coursework I’m behind, and the basic stuff at home—bills, meals, chores—keeps piling up. I just don’t follow through very well right now. My spouse has been handling more, and I’ve kind of stepped back from friends and art commitments too.
Would you say that your low mood and lack of interest in activities are causing significant distress or impairment in your daily life most days?

Yeah… most days, I think. I’m behind on my certificate work, and normal things like bills, meals, house stuff just kind of pile up. My spouse has had to take on more, and I haven’t really been keeping up with friends or art commitments.
